Experience

Research & training

My training spans cardiovascular mechanobiology, vascular redox biology, and chronic inflammation.

View CV ↗

Research experience

  1. 2023 to present

    Robert J. Levy Laboratory

    University of Pennsylvania · Philadelphia, PA

    Graduate research on PIEZO1 activation, serotonin signaling, and mitral valve remodeling. I use human valve cell models, controlled mechanical stimulation, and molecular assays to investigate how mechanical cues affect cellular behavior.

  2. Summer 2024

    Emanuela Bruscia Laboratory

    Yale University · New Haven, CT

    Studied CCR2+ monocyte migration and differentiation during chronic lung inflammation using mouse models and multicolor flow cytometry.

  3. 2019 to 2023

    Jingyan Han Laboratory

    Boston University · Boston, MA

    Investigated vascular redox dysregulation, atherosclerosis, and thoracic aortic aneurysm biology, with work on vascular remodeling and translational disease models.

Experimental toolkit

Cell & molecular biology

Primary cell culture, RNA extraction, RT-qPCR, western blotting, ELISA, siRNA knockdown, and immunofluorescence.

Models & phenotyping

Controlled mechanical stimulation, flow cytometry, mouse models, single-cell suspension, and in-gel zymography.

Analysis & visualization

FlowJo, GraphPad Prism, ImageJ, R, and BioRender.
